# Standards & federation

Filinq declares the standards below in its manifest. OpenRegister publishes them to other servers without login, under `filinq.discovery` in `/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities`, so another instance can tell from a hostname alone whether it can connect. Tools such as [Nextcloud Peek](https://genhttp.dev/lambda/nextcloud-peek/) show it too.

## Standards this app provides

| Standard | Version | Access | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| [PDF/A-3b archival PDF (conversion and rendering, embedded attachments, veraPDF-checked)](https://www.iso.org/standard/57229.html) | 3b | Nextcloud login | `/apps/filinq/api/pdfa3` (not published) |

## Standards this app uses

None.

## Federation (Open Cloud Mesh)

Filinq registers no Open Cloud Mesh resource type of its own. Objects it stores in OpenRegister can still be shared with another instance through OpenRegister's `openregister` resource type.

## How another server finds this

```bash
curl -s -H 'OCS-APIRequest: true' \
  'https://cloud.example.org/ocs/v2.php/cloud/capabilities?format=json' \
  | jq '.ocs.data.capabilities["filinq"].discovery'
```

Paths are relative to the instance root. Prefix `/index.php` when the instance runs without pretty URLs (`core.mod-rewrite-working` is false). Endpoints that need a Nextcloud login are listed without their path.

## Administrators

- Stop publishing discovery for every app: `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_public --value=no`
- Hide only this app: add `filinq` to `occ config:app:set openregister discovery_hidden_apps --value=...` (comma separated)

Field reference and the shared list of standard ids: [Discovery and federation](https://github.com/ConductionNL/openregister/blob/development/docs/Technical/discovery-and-federation.md).
